en: I am going to the office now.
context: Telling someone where you are headed.
explain: Use 'the' before office when you mean your workplace. Do not say 'going to office'.

en: He knows the answer.
context: Talking about someone who has the answer.
explain: Do not say 'is knowing'. Know is a state verb, so we use the simple present.

en: We discussed the plan yesterday.
tamil: நேத்து நாங்க அந்த திட்டத்தை பத்தி பேசினோம்.
context: Reporting a meeting at work.
explain: Do not say 'discuss about'. Discuss already means talk about, so no 'about'.

en: She is trying to cope with the stress.
tamil: அவ அந்த மன அழுத்தத்தை சமாளிக்க முயற்சி பண்ணிட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Talking about a friend under pressure.
explain: Do not say 'cope up'. The correct phrase is 'cope with'.

en: Can we move the meeting to an earlier time?
context: Asking a colleague to reschedule earlier.
explain: 'Prepone' is not standard English. Say 'move it earlier' or 'bring it forward'.

en: I have lived in Chennai for ten years.
context: Telling someone how long you have lived somewhere.
explain: Use 'for' with a length of time (ten years). Do not say 'since ten years'.

en: I have been waiting since morning.
context: Complaining politely about a long wait.
explain: Use 'since' with a starting point (morning). Use present perfect, not 'I am waiting since'.

en: Please explain the rules to me.
context: Asking a teacher or manager for help.
explain: Say 'explain something to someone'. Do not say 'explain me'.

en: My friend gave me some good advice.
tamil: என் நண்பன் எனக்கு நல்ல அறிவுரை சொன்னான்.
context: Thanking or talking about helpful guidance.
explain: Advice is uncountable. Do not say 'advices'; say 'some advice' or 'a piece of advice'.

en: The information you sent is very useful.
tamil: நீங்க அனுப்பின தகவல் ரொம்ப பயனுள்ளதா இருக்கு.
context: Replying to an email with details.
explain: Information is uncountable, so it takes 'is', never 'informations'.

en: She is married to a teacher.
context: Talking about someone's spouse.
explain: We say 'married to' someone. Do not say 'married with'.

en: I am good at maths.
context: Talking about your strengths in school or interviews.
explain: Use 'good at' for a skill. Do not say 'good in maths'.

en: My sister is afraid of dogs.
context: Talking about a fear.
explain: Use 'afraid of' something. Do not say 'afraid from'.

en: What time does the train leave?
context: Asking at the station.
explain: In questions use 'does' plus the base verb. Do not say 'what time the train leaves?'.

en: I don't have any money with me.
context: Telling a friend you cannot pay right now.
explain: Use 'any' in negative sentences. 'I have no money' also works, but 'any' sounds more natural here.

en: He told me that he was busy.
tamil: அவன் தான் பிஸியா இருக்கேன்னு என்கிட்ட சொன்னான்.
context: Reporting what someone said.
explain: 'Tell' needs a person after it (told me). Use 'said' when there is no person.

alt.en: He said that he was busy.

en: I have already finished my lunch.
context: Telling a colleague you have eaten.
explain: Use present perfect with 'already'. Do not say 'I already finished' in careful English.

en: I am looking forward to meeting you.
context: Ending a polite email or message.
explain: After 'look forward to' use the -ing form. Do not say 'look forward to meet'.

en: Everyone is waiting for you.
context: Calling someone who is late.
explain: Everyone is singular, so use 'is'. Do not say 'everyone are'.

en: The news is good today.
context: Sharing good updates.
explain: News is uncountable and singular. Do not say 'the news are' or 'a news'.

en: I live in Madurai with my parents.
tamil: நான் மதுரையில என் அப்பா அம்மா கூட இருக்கேன்.
context: Introducing yourself.
explain: Use 'live' for your home. 'Stay' usually means a short visit, like in a hotel.

alt.en: I am staying in a hotel this week.
alt.tamil: நான் இந்த வாரம் ஒரு ஹோட்டல்ல தங்கியிருக்கேன்.
